source: geoBoundaries gbOpen ADM1
dataset: administrative boundary
coverage: country admin level 1; filtered by name
access: public HTTP
limitations: Open boundary dataset, not a cadastral/legal parcel boundary.

source: NASA POWER Daily API
dataset: daily gridded meteorological estimates
coverage: 38 project grid points; 2017-01-01 to 2026-10-25; 8 daily variables. The 2024-2026 extension was requested one calendar-year chunk per point and retained as raw JSON and processed CSV.
access: public HTTP
limitations: NASA POWER gridded/model estimates, not field station observations. Daily API default local solar time (LST). 2026 is a partial near-real-time year and may be revised or delayed; retain sentinels as NULL. No imagery or vegetation indices included.

source: ISRIC SoilGrids REST API v2.0
dataset: soil property point queries
coverage: one successful clay-value test point; one null point and a multi-property timeout; no SoilGrids values were merged into the project
access: public HTTP, fair-use limit applies
limitations: Point values are modelled predictions with uncertainty at 250 m, not field tests. Coverage and unit conversions must be checked before importing; current project test did not establish complete Kafr El Sheikh coverage.

source: Copernicus Data Space STAC Catalog
dataset: Sentinel-2 L2A scene metadata
coverage: scene footprints intersecting admin boundary and date window
access: public catalog search
limitations: Catalog records are not image downloads. Actual imagery processing/download may require OAuth credentials and quota.

source: Egypt Ministry of Agriculture
dataset: official rice area/production/irrigation records
coverage: not automatically collected by this starter because no stable documented public API was verified
access: manual/source-specific
limitations: No official production numbers are fabricated; import verified tables when available.

source: CAPMAS Agricultural Areas Bulletin 2019/2020
dataset: rice area and production by governorate, 2019/2020
coverage: Kafr El Sheikh area and production; yield in regional_stats is computed as production divided by area
access: public CAPMAS statistical bulletin PDF
limitations: The bulletin reports cereal-crop area and production, not yield; the database derives yield from those reported values.

source: Agricultural Research Center - Field Crops Research Institute product catalogue
dataset: published rice variety attributes
coverage: catalogue entries for selected rice varieties; retrieved traits are stored in rice_variety_reference_arc.csv
access: public web catalogue
limitations: Published yield ranges are catalogue figures, not guaranteed farm outcomes or local measurements.

source: Agricultural Research Center - Rice Research Department product catalogue
dataset: published rice cultivar descriptions, growth duration, catalogue yield ranges, grain type, disease notes, soil suitability, and temperature range
coverage: 18 rice catalogue profiles with published traits transcribed to rice_variety_reference_arc.csv
access: public ARC product catalogue; curated CSV extract
limitations: Catalogue traits and yield ranges are not field guarantees or proof of current seed approval. ARC catalogue pages conflict for Sakha 109 yield and plant type; disputed traits are withheld. No irrigation requirement or Kafr El Sheikh planting calendar is provided by this extract.

source: Journal of Plant Production - Ghazy, Mikhael, and El-Refaee (2019)
dataset: Giza 179 station-trial grain yield and water productivity under three irrigation intervals and four plant spacings
coverage: Sakha Research Station, Kafr El-Sheikh; seasons 2017 and 2018; 48 treatment-result observations
access: Open journal PDF; DOI 10.21608/jpp.2019.77743; curated transcription
limitations: Small research-station plots, not farmer-field records. The extracted tables report water productivity but not absolute treatment irrigation volumes; do not use for pump run-time calculations.

source: CAPMAS agricultural indicators
dataset: rice cultivated area and production indicators
coverage: annual agricultural indicators; exact geographic and downloadable series availability must be checked per indicator
access: public indicator page; series downloads may require page interaction
limitations: Use only the geographic level and years explicitly shown by the source; do not derive field-level labels from governorate totals.

source: FAO WaPOR
dataset: evapotranspiration/water productivity products
coverage: WaPOR v3 continental/national products; the FAO data-access page documents Level 1/2 collections and an API without an API key. Product-specific Kafr El Sheikh spatial and temporal coverage still needs to be extracted and checked.
access: Public FAO WaPOR v3 API; no credentials required per FAO access documentation
limitations: Remote-sensing-derived ET/water productivity products, not farmer-metered irrigation. Check spatial support, resolution, product version, latency, and Kafr El Sheikh coverage before import; do not treat AET as applied irrigation volume.

source: Suteksan Egypt pump catalogue
dataset: SEP 6/7/8-inch submersible pump series family ranges
coverage: Six frequency-specific catalogue rows transcribed to pump_catalog_suteksan.csv
access: Public manufacturer pages
limitations: Published family limits are not matched flow/head duty points; they do not establish farm discharge or run time.

source: Egypt Ministry of Agriculture, Economic Affairs Sector (2023)
dataset: Table 93 stationary/mobile irrigation pump census
coverage: One row labelled Kafr El Sheikh transcribed to machinery_inventory_ministry.csv
access: Public official PDF table extract
limitations: The row's exact administrative level is ambiguous in the extracted table and must be confirmed before joining to district records; aggregate counts are not a farmer machine catalogue.

source: Agricultural Research Center - Rice technical recommendation bulletin (2026)
dataset: Rice recommendation excerpts from the ARC page and its PDF attachment
coverage: 18 ARC-specific rules and 5 Ministry-attributed nursery rules in rice_recommendations_arc.csv, including climate-adaptation cultivar list, method-scoped dry direct-seeding calendar, irrigation intervals, and fertilizer rules
access: Public ARC page and indexed attachment excerpts
limitations: The full attachment was not downloaded and parsed end-to-end; these are excerpts from indexed sections, tagged official_pdf_excerpt. Method-specific dry direct-seeding rules must not be applied to transplanted rice; salinity-only rules remain scoped, and fertilizer formulation must be checked before farm use.

source: El-Henawy (2013), Kafrelsheikh University farm rice/previous-crop soil trial
dataset: Published soil and rice treatment means for wheat-rice and berseem-rice sequences, puddling treatments, and two soil depths
coverage: Kafrelsheikh University Faculty of Agriculture farm; 2007 rice season; 104 transcribed values from Tables 1-5
access: Open journal PDF
limitations: One research-farm location and one season; grouped treatment means, not parcel-level measurements. Rice-yield treatment differences were reported as statistically non-significant. Use as local research evidence only, not as a fertilizer or field-soil prediction.

source: Gewaily et al. (2018), Sakha RRTC rice soil nutrient baseline
dataset: Published soil texture, pH, EC, organic matter, total N, available P/K/Zn at the Sakha rice research farm
coverage: Two pre-plant baseline years, 2016 and 2017; 20 property-year observations transcribed from Table 1
access: Open journal PDF
limitations: Single experimental station; sampling depth and parcel coordinates are not reported with the table. Published baseline is not a current field test and does not by itself define nutrient deficiency thresholds.

source: Yageta et al. (2013), previous rice history and salinity near Sakha
dataset: Study-level evidence from 15 sites on prior two-year rice history, soil salinity, drainage and irrigation-water quality
coverage: One ARC site and 14 private farms within 5 km of Sakha RRTC; soils sampled at 0-20 cm in May 2010
access: Open J-STAGE journal PDF
limitations: Observational grouped study with no public parcel-level raw data. Prior rice frequency was not a significant salt-accumulation factor in this sample; area, subsurface drainage and irrigation-water quality mattered. Do not generalize as parcel-level cause or prediction.

source: Local crop-name and season normalization for Kafr El-Sheikh
dataset: Arabic/English canonical labels, botanical names, typical season and crop functional group for seven common crops
coverage: Rice, wheat, Egyptian clover, maize, cotton, sugar beet, and barley
access: Curated ETL lookup based on local crop context and local Sakha trial terminology
limitations: Normalization and feature engineering only. Legume/cereal group is not a numerical nutrient-credit or fertilizer recommendation.

source: Ibrahim (2002), rice following berseem or wheat at Tag El-Ezz, Dakahlia
dataset: Two-season Sakha 101 station experiment with soil N/P/K after prior winter crop and grain-yield means by preceding crop
coverage: Tag El-Ezz Agricultural Research Station, Dakahlia; summer seasons 2000 and 2001; berseem vs wheat; four replicates
access: Open journal PDF
limitations: Neighboring Delta comparison, not Kafr El-Sheikh. Older station trial with nutrient/fertilizer interactions; do not transfer its soil values or fertilizer rates as current field recommendations.

source: Egypt Agricultural Portal - May 2025 rice recommendations
dataset: Variety-specific cultivation guide and nursery recommendations attributed to the Ministry of Agriculture extension sector
coverage: 13 cultivar rows and nursery/seed rules transcribed in the processed CSVs
access: Public agricultural extension portal; article identifies the Ministry extension sector as issuer
limitations: A dated repost of Ministry recommendations, not a current seed-availability list. Keep separate from ARC catalogue values; yield is a bulletin claim, not a local guarantee.

source: Darwesh, Abdelkhalek and Ibrahim (2016), rice irrigation periods and submerged depths in North Nile Delta
dataset: 2013-2014 Sakha station trial: seasonal applied irrigation, yield, irrigation-water productivity, thousand-grain weight by variety/interval/depth; soil profile 0-60 cm; monthly station climate summaries
coverage: Sakha Agricultural Research Station Farm, Kafr El-Sheikh; varieties Giza 177, Sakha 101, Orabi 1; 6/12 day interval; ponding 3/5/7 cm; 3 replications
access: Open journal PDF; Tables 1-4 transcribed into data/processed/darwesh_sakha_irrigation_trial_2013_2014.csv and literature_trial_observation
limitations: Single historical research-station site, not farmer-field labels. Seasonal water includes nursery, land preparation, and establishment. Treatment results are not pump runtime instructions. No DOI was recorded because it was not confirmed from the source page.

source: Moursi and Abdelkhalek (2015), water requirement components of Egyptian rice varieties in North Nile Delta
dataset: Sakha 2012-2013 climate summaries; irrigation/water-budget components; ETa lysimeter measurements, ETo/ETc method comparisons, and seasonal water/yield/productivity summaries for Giza 178, Sakha 102, Sakha 104
coverage: Sakha Agricultural Research Station, Kafr El-Sheikh; two summer seasons 2012 and 2013; 144 transcribed observations from Tables 1, 3, 4, 5 and results text
access: Open journal PDF; DOI 10.21608/asejaiqjsae.2015.2859; curated CSV extract and literature_trial_observation
limitations: Research-station evidence, not farm labels. Contains two-season averages and per-year monthly weather. The source describes rainfall/runoff/drainage data as unavailable or negligible in its balance. Wind speed units are inconsistent in the article and are stored as ambiguous; keep source-reported units and qualifiers.

source: Ghazy, Hashem and Sheta (2024), Sakha 106 irrigation/compost/potassium-silicate trial
dataset: 2022-2023 Sakha station Table 8: total irrigation water, yield, water saved and WUE for 4-, 8-, 12-day irrigation marginal means
coverage: Sakha Agricultural Research Station, Kafr El-Sheikh; Sakha 106; three replications; factorial compost and potassium-silicate trial; 22 numeric table observations transcribed
access: Open journal PDF; DOI 10.21608/jenvbs.2024.302891.1252; curated CSV and literature_trial_observation
limitations: Station trial, not farmer field labels. Table 8 provides irrigation-interval marginal means across fertilizer treatments, not fertilizer-by-irrigation cell means. Total water is m3/ha and cannot be converted to pump run time without actual pump duty conditions.

source: Eid et al. (2025), planting methods and irrigation depth in Northern Nile Delta rice
dataset: 2023-2024 treatment table: applied irrigation, grain yield and water productivity for traditional/furrow/bed planting × 7/5/3 cm irrigation depth
coverage: Northern Nile Delta study; exact station and cultivar not captured in the extracted Table 3 data; 54 numeric cells transcribed
access: Open Egyptian Journal of Soil Science PDF; DOI 10.21608/ejss.2025.410842.2305
limitations: Keep at Northern Delta regional study support until exact site/cultivar are verified from full methods. Treatment means are not farmer labels or parcel-specific Kafr El-Sheikh recommendations.

source: Basiouny et al. (2020), reuse of agricultural wastewater for rice in Kafr El-Sheikh
dataset: Five irrigation-water blend cases, rice water needs, production, water-use efficiency and field water/soil salinity during 2018 summer season
coverage: Meet Yazeed canal fresh water blended with private-drain water in Kafr El-Sheikh; precise field coordinates and complete numeric tables not yet extracted
access: Open Engineering Research Journal PDF; DOI 10.21608/erjsh.2020.405610; extraction pending
limitations: Field study in the governorate, but keep as study-site measurements and do not project to all fields or water sources. Numeric table rows and units must be transcribed and checked before import.

source: Abou El Hassan (2017), water deficit at critical rice growth stages at El-Karada
dataset: 2014-2015 station study of continuous flooding and 12-day water withholding at mid-tillering, panicle initiation and heading; Table 8 reports seasonal water, yield, yield reduction, water saving and WUE
coverage: El-Karada Research Station, Kafr El-Sheikh; 36 values transcribed from Table 8 into data/processed/abou_el_hassan_karada_water_deficit_2014_2015.csv and literature_trial_observation; irrigation means across three cultivars
access: Open Journal of Soil Science and Agricultural Engineering PDF; DOI 10.21608/jssae.2017.37229; Table 8 transcription script included
limitations: Research-station treatment means, not farmer records or cultivar-specific output. The 2014 mid-tillering water-saving value is 6.33% in Table 8 but 6.37% in the abstract; the table value is stored and discrepancy documented. Do not use as a farm pump-runtime prediction.

source: Agricultural Pesticides Committee (APC), approved pest-control recommendations, 2025 edition
dataset: Official recommendations and registered pesticide-use list, including crop-specific rice material; detailed table extraction not completed
coverage: The 2025 edition is announced by the Ministry's APC; rice page/table numbers and entries remain to be verified from the official book
access: Official APC PDF endpoint identified; PDF fetch was unavailable to the current reader. The APC announcement page is https://www.apc.gov.eg/AR/News.aspx?id=10226. Discovery notice: https://alfallahalyoum.news/لجنة-المبيدات-تتيح-دليل-مكافحة-الآفات-20.html/
limitations: The 2025 book is not proof of current 2026 registration. Extract official rice crop pages and verify every product/use, dose, pre-harvest interval, and registration status before importing or displaying spray advice.

source: Agricultural Pesticides Committee (APC), rice pest/disease entries in the 2025 approved recommendations (secondary transcription)
dataset: Five rice pest/disease symptom and timing reference records (bloodworms, blast, false smut, bakanae, nematode white-tip)
coverage: Rice only; pages 41-44 attributed to the APC 2025 booklet; copied from secondary pages that identify APC as author/source
access: Official primary PDF identified but not readable through current retrieval; secondary transcripts searched and attributed to APC 2025
limitations: No pesticide product, active ingredient, dose, or pre-harvest interval imported. Secondary transcription only; verify against the official APC booklet before operational use. Reference-only, not spray advice.

source: Kafrelsheikh University repository, Amgad Ahmed Essa Rehan thesis abstract (2013)
dataset: Two abstract-level grain-yield results for GZ 9057 transplanted on 15 April at Sakha: 4.31 t/feddan in 2012 and 4.65 t/feddan in 2013; trial compared three sowing dates and two planting methods
coverage: Experimental farm of Sakha Agriculture Research Station, Kafr El-Sheikh; summer seasons 2012-2013
access: Public university repository PDF; result transcribed from p.19 abstract into processed CSV and literature_evidence
limitations: Abstract-only result from a DUS experiment; not a typical farm yield, current cultivar availability confirmation, or guaranteed recommendation. It must not be treated as a local farm label.

source: Gaber et al. (2025), Sakha irrigation water quality, soil quality and rice grain metals
dataset: Tables 10-14: 398 numeric records for yield, grain traits and grain mineral/heavy-metal composition across 2022/2023, 4 cultivars and five water treatments; plus 3 abstract-level evidence statements.
coverage: Two Sakha Agriculture Research Station summer trials, 2022 and 2023; four replicates; Giza 183, Giza 178, Sakha 106 and Sakha 108
access: Publisher-indexed PDF full-text; numeric results transcribed into data/processed/sakha_water_quality_2022_2023_numeric_results.csv and literature_trial_result.
limitations: Water and soil chemistry tables remain untranscribed. Grain mineral/heavy-metal values are treatment means from one research station, not farmer-field values or a standalone food-safety determination; water mixes are not universal blend recommendations.

source: El-Hadidi et al. (2008), Irrigation Water Management of Rice Crop in North Delta
dataset: 24 numeric results: total irrigation water applied and grain yield for six Sakha 104 transplanting layouts across 2006 and 2007 seasons
coverage: El-Karada Water Requirements Research Station, Kafr El-Sheikh; 3 replicates; plot area 320 m2; six transplanting methods
access: Open journal article indexed by EKB; tables 1-2 transcribed into CSV and literature_trial_result. ResearchGate copy also provides indexed full-text.
limitations: Research-station trial from 2006-2007; not farmer labels or a current blanket recommendation. Do not conflate with another similarly themed Meleha et al. study. No pump runtime inferred.

source: Eid et al. (2022), Hammoul rice soil and irrigation-water chemistry
dataset: Published baseline soil chemistry, irrigation-water chemistry, and reported water-quality indices
coverage: Hammoul District; two rice seasons 2020 and 2021; soil before cultivation and blended canal/drainage water samples
access: Public publisher PDF; DOI 10.21608/jssae.2022.124127.1056
limitations: Experimental-site observations only; not a spatial layer or farmer field measurements. Transcribed Tables 1, 2, and 4; Table 5 omitted because reported baseline EC values conflict. Values do not determine irrigation volume or pump runtime.

source: ARC Rice Research Department, Sakha Super 300 product page
dataset: Cultivar attributes and maturity duration by planting timing
coverage: Sakha Super 300 cultivar; official ARC product page
access: Public ARC page
limitations: The source reports different duration for early versus late planting (147 versus 114 days); this is not a single fixed season length.

source: El-Banna et al. (2023), Kafr El-Sheikh geotechnical maps
dataset: 119 borehole investigations and interpolated spatial summaries including groundwater depth
coverage: Kafr El-Sheikh Governorate; geotechnical boreholes with depth up to 20–30 m
access: Public Open Geosciences article
limitations: Area classes are a published interpolated map summary, not parcel-level agricultural groundwater monitoring. Reported mapped area 3835.461 km2 conflicts with article-stated governorate area 3716.68 km2. Do not use as field-specific groundwater depth.
